# Part 10 — Real Shopify query examples generated by the LLM

Source: real run, `openai`/`gpt-5.6-luna`, 2026-08-25, no prewritten GraphQL supplied — the model was
given only the natural-language task "how would you query active products, their variants, and
inventory availability at each location?" plus the `shopify_schema`/`shopify_query` tool
definitions. Full transcript: `.context/agentic-shopify-gateway/latest.json`. Reproduced verbatim.

## The GraphQL document the model wrote (turn 6, validated on first attempt — no reject/repair needed)

```graphql
query ActiveProductsInventory($first: Int!, $locationFirst: Int!) {
  products(first: $first, query: "status:active") {
    nodes {
      id
      title
      status
      variants(first: $first) {
        nodes {
          id
          title
          sku
          inventoryItem {
            id
            tracked
            inventoryLevels(first: $locationFirst) {
              nodes {
                location {
                  id
                  name
                  isActive
                }
                quantities(names: ["available"]) {
                  name
                  quantity
                }
              }
            }
          }
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Variables: `{"first": 100, "locationFirst": 100}`

This passed `analyzeGatewayDocument()` structural validation (query-only, single operation, depth/
node/pagination limits, no disallowed directives) without a single rejection. It correctly uses
`InventoryLevel.quantities(names: [...])` — the current, non-deprecated way to read available
inventory — rather than the older `available` scalar field, which is a small but real signal that the
model's underlying Shopify domain knowledge, not just the local schema index, is contributing.

## What happened when it tried to execute it

```
"No live Shopify token configured in this environment (JEFE_GOLDEN_PATH_SHOPIFY_ADMIN_ACCESS_TOKEN
is unset). This is an honest failure, not simulated data."
```

This is the deliberately unmocked failure path (see `13-known-limitations.md`) — the eval script
refuses to fabricate a plausible-looking Shopify response. The model's turn-7 final answer correctly
reported that the live request failed and no data was retrieved, rather than presenting the query
result as real evidence. That itself is a useful data point: the honest-failure design didn't get
silently swallowed or hallucinated past.

## Schema discovery path that got it there

The model tried four different discovery strategies across turns 0–5 before landing on a document it
was confident enough to run:

1. Broad keyword `search` across all the concepts it expected to need (turn 0–2).
2. `inspect_field` on object **type** names (`Product`, `ProductVariant`, `InventoryItem`...) — this
   **failed** (`FIELD_NOT_FOUND`) because `shopify_schema`'s `inspect_field` only resolves root
   Query/Mutation field names, not arbitrary object types. Real, useful evidence of a genuine gap —
   see `13-known-limitations.md`.
3. `list_fields` to enumerate available root query names.
4. A final, more targeted `search` pass, after which it wrote the query above directly rather than
   inspecting further.

This is the schema-discovery-and-repair loop the task brief asked to prove, observed directly rather
than asserted: the model adapted its strategy when a tool call failed, without any special prompting
for that specific failure mode.
